basis: Collecting-duct cysts and congenital hepatic fibrosis define ARPKD; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Hypertension and hypersplenism are secondary effects.
Acquired cyst located in the kidney; no evidence of other organ involvement.
Necrotizing vasculitis; neuropathy occurs in ~50-70% and renal ischemic involvement in ~40-60%. Skin (~30-50%) and bowel involvement omitted by cap.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss with vestibular dysfunction in 2/2 patients; both affect the ear.
Premature ovarian failure is loss of gonadal endocrine function, rather than isolated reproductive infertility.
Inherited hemoglobin oxidation disorder. Destructive CNS findings are occasional and concentrated in type II; the broad frequent neurologic annotation does not establish common damage.
Sarcoma arising in bone; metastatic sites are not defining organ involvement.
Abnormal dilation of vessels defines the umbrella; particular skin or gastrointestinal sites are subtype-specific.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and defining jaw/digital skeletal and eye abnormalities; individual ocular findings occur in 1-2/7 patients, but the eye is a named syndrome component.
Spastic neuropathy with mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation dysfunction; visual loss/scotoma and lower-limb muscle atrophy occur in 2/2, with optic atrophy documented.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with acephalic spermatozoa; reproductive dysfunction without demonstrated gonadal hormone failure.
Follicular keratin plugging and dry skin define this cutaneous disorder.
Both listed subtypes cause CNS abnormalities or neurodegeneration; dysosteosclerosis belongs to a rare subtype and does not characterize most patients.
Mandibulofacial skeletal dysostosis and intellectual disability define the syndrome; no supplied evidence supports additional organs.
Inherited glycolytic enzyme deficiency; typically asymptomatic, with no demonstrated muscle or other organ damage despite the glycogen-storage name.
Inherited atrial arrhythmia defines the disease. Stroke occurred in 3/6 patients but is a separately diagnosed embolic complication.
Spastic motor neuropathy within P5CS deficiency; persistent pes cavus affects 30-79%, with distal weakness in 15/16. Cataracts and hearing loss are occasional.
Congenital protein glycosylation disorder with global developmental delay in 12/12 patients. Reflux and individual functional eye abnormalities are below 30%.
Multinodular enlargement of the thyroid is an endocrine-gland disorder even when thyroid hormone function remains normal.
External/middle-ear malformations with conductive hearing loss; hypogonadism and global developmental delay each occur in 30-79%.
Inherited demyelinating/axonal peripheral neuropathy; persistent distal lower-limb muscle wasting occurs in 7/7 patients, with characteristic foot deformities.
Vertebral and epiphyseal skeletal dysplasia with flattened bone ends and premature osteoarthritis.
Intellectual disability and skeletal dysplasia/osteopoikilosis define the syndrome. Pigmentation alone does not establish skin damage; renal anomalies occur in 5-29%.
Antibody-associated autoimmune cerebellar dysfunction defines both the neurologic site and immune mechanism.
Nevi/lipoatrophy and T-cell deficiency; cataract/visual loss and cognitive/thalamic abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Cap omits endocrine, skeletal, dental, hepatic and cardiac involvement.
